title: Daksha Mahadev Temple Haridwar | History, Timings & Travel Guide
content:
Daksha Mahadev Temple - Haridwar,

The Daksha Mahadev Temple (also called Daksheshwar Mahadev Temple) is one of the most ancient and significant temples in Haridwar, dedicated to Lord Shiva. Located in the Kankhal area, about 4 km from Har Ki Pauri, this temple holds immense religious importance due to its association with the famous mythological story of Daksha Yagna.

According to Hindu mythology, King Daksha Prajapati, father of Goddess Sati (wife of Lord Shiva), organized a grand yagna (sacrificial ritual) at this very place. However, Daksha insulted Lord Shiva by not inviting him. Feeling deeply hurt, Sati immolated herself in the sacrificial fire. Enraged, Shiva unleashed his fierce form Veerbhadra, who destroyed the yagna and beheaded Daksha. Later, on the request of the gods, Shiva forgave Daksha and restored his life by placing a goat’s head on him.

This temple marks that legendary spot and is considered a symbol of faith, devotion, and divine forgiveness. Pilgrims visit to offer prayers to Lord Shiva and to connect with this powerful mythological past. The temple is especially crowded during Shivratri and the Shravan month, when devotees gather in huge numbers to worship Mahadev.

The serene surroundings of Kankhal, combined with the temple’s mythological significance, make Daksha Mahadev Temple not only a place of worship but also a cultural landmark for visitors exploring Haridwar.

How to Reach Daksha Mahadev Temple:

  • By Road: 4 km from Haridwar city center/Har Ki Pauri, easy by auto, taxi, or rickshaw.
  • By Train: Haridwar Junction is the nearest station, just 3 km away.
  • By Air: Jolly Grant Airport (Dehradun) is 35 km from Haridwar.
